subject_entity.notes: Irenaeus of Lyons's five-book refutation of Gnosticism c. 180, establishing apostolic succession, rule of faith, and the fourfold Gospel as the standard against Valentinian and Marcionite innovations.

object_entity.proposition_label: Old Testament is Authoritative Scripture
object_entity.description: The Church accepts the Old Testament as authoritative Christian scripture; the God of creation and Israel is the same God as the Father of Jesus Christ. Denied by Marcion, Valentinus, Basilides, and most Gnostic schools.

evidence.notes: Irenaeus argues from OT as Christian scripture against those who separate the two Testaments.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: When confuted from the Scriptures, heretics accuse them of being incorrect or ambiguous and claim truth was delivered by word of mouth alone; when referred to the apostolic tradition preserved by the succession of presbyters in the Churches, they object to that too — they consent neither to Scripture nor to tradition.

source.notes: Five-book refutation of Gnosticism; ANF Vol. 1 translation by Roberts and Rambaut, revised for New Advent by Kevin Knight.

object_entity.proposition_label: Christ Truly Suffered and Died
object_entity.description: Christ's passion and death on the cross were genuine physical events, not apparent, symbolic, or borne by a substitute. Denied by docetists, Basilides (Simon Cyrene substitution), Marcion, and Cerinthus.

evidence.notes: Irenaeus AH 5.2.2-3 argues Christ's true bodily flesh was given for us, refuting docetic denials.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: If the flesh cannot be saved then the Lord did not redeem us with His blood; but the cup of the Eucharist is the communion of His blood and the bread the communion of His body. The bread and cup, receiving the Word of God, become the body and blood of Christ by which our flesh is nourished; and our bodies, nourished by the eucharist and deposited in the earth, shall rise at their appointed time, the Word of God granting them resurrection to the glory of God the Father.

object_entity.proposition_label: Baptismal Anointing with Oil
object_entity.description: After emerging from the baptismal water, the newly baptized is anointed with chrism or oil as part of the baptismal rite, signifying the reception of the Holy Spirit and incorporation into Christ.

passage.excerpt: This Spirit did descend upon the Lord as a dove; upon us also the same Spirit descended when we were baptized. And just as He who was born of a virgin became Christ, so we too, by birth through the Spirit, become sons of God and fellow-heirs with Christ.
passage.notes: Baptism gives the Holy Spirit; the baptism of believers parallels the anointing of Christ

object_entity.proposition_label: Ordination is conferred by the laying on of hands
object_entity.description: The ministry of bishop, presbyter, and deacon is conferred through the liturgical act of laying on of hands by existing bishops (for episcopal ordination) or by the bishop (for presbyters and deacons).

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: It is within the power of all in every Church to contemplate the tradition of the apostles manifested throughout the whole world and to reckon up those who were instituted bishops by the apostles and their succession to our own times; those who taught nothing like what the heretics rave about.

object_entity.proposition_label: Faith is transmitted through apostolic succession
object_entity.description: The bishops who succeed the apostles are authoritative guarantors of the received tradition.

evidence.notes: AH 3.1.1: salvation plan learned through those who brought the Gospel — apostolic chain.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: We learned the plan of salvation from those through whom the Gospel came to us. Matthew issued a written Gospel among the Hebrews while Peter and Paul were preaching at Rome. Mark, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, handed down what Peter had preached. Luke, Paul's companion, recorded his Gospel. Afterwards John, who leaned on the Lord's breast, published his Gospel during his residence at Ephesus.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The tradition derived from the apostles of the very great, very ancient, universally known Church founded at Rome by Peter and Paul — every Church must agree with this Church on account of its preeminent authority (potiorem principalitatem); the faith preached to men comes down to our time by means of the successions of the bishops.

source.title: Against Heresies
source.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
source.notes: Five-book refutation of Gnosticism; ANF Vol. 1 translation by Roberts and Rambaut, revised for New Advent by Kevin Knight.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The Rome bishop succession: Peter and Paul committed the episcopate to Linus; then Anacletus; then Clement (third from the apostles, who had seen the blessed apostles); then Evaristus, Alexander, Sixtus, Telephorus (gloriously martyred), Hyginus, Pius, Anicetus, Soter, and Eleutherius (twelfth from the apostles, now in office). In this order and by this succession the ecclesiastical tradition from the apostles and the preaching of the truth have come down to us.
